# Case Study: FlowOps

## Late deliveries down 60%

*Sector: read from your inputs as logistics tech. Business model: not stated. Tell us how you charge and the plan will adjust.*

Any priced offer below requires a written quote and buyer agreement.

*Built from: challenge: given; solution: given; results: 3 items (3 outcomes); customer quote: given; industry: given.*

---

## The Story (draft)

**The situation.** FlowOps is in the Logistics segment. (General note for logistics tech, not from your inputs: teams are usually judged on on time delivery and cost per shipment or per order.)

**The challenge.** Before RouteIQ, the team was dealing with this, in your words: dispatchers spent four hours a day planning routes by hand and late deliveries hit 18 percent.

**The approach.** The team brought in RouteIQ. RouteIQ planned routes automatically and sent drivers live updates.

**The result.** Late deliveries down 60%. Planning time cut from 4 hours to 30 minutes. 12% lower fuel cost.

**In their words.** "We got our afternoons back." That is how FlowOps sums it up.

*The sections below hold the detail behind each part of the story and the questions that finish it.*

## The Challenge

What the team was dealing with: Dispatchers spent four hours a day planning routes by hand and late deliveries hit 18 percent.

**Before publication, the account owner should confirm with the customer:**
- What the problem cost them, with the starting value of one of: on time delivery, cost per shipment or per order and order cycle time.
- Interview question in the sector's language: "Which systems hold your orders, shipments and stock today, and who owns the data in them?"

---

## The Solution

What was put in place: RouteIQ planned routes automatically and sent drivers live updates.

**Before publication, the account owner should verify:**
- Why FlowOps chose RouteIQ, and which alternative it weighed (a common reaction in logistics tech: "We already have a system for this").
- How the rollout went, and how long it took to see first results. Use only a duration the customer confirms.
- Words to use as the customer says them: shipment, carrier, consignment, lead time, exception.

---

## The Results

**Outcomes**

- Late deliveries down 60%.
- Planning time cut from 4 hours to 30 minutes.
- 12% lower fuel cost.

**Before publication, the evidence owner should check each figure:** record the value before, the value after and the measurement period. A strong proof point here: A before and after of on time delivery or cost per shipment on one lane, site or region, measured over a full cycle of busy and quiet weeks. Measures of this sector that the results do not yet show: on time delivery, cost per shipment or per order, order cycle time and exception rate. Add one if the customer tracks it.

## Where This Goes Next

Before changing your process, record the starting point for RouteIQ in one comparable case. Agree the measure and review period with the person who owns the work, then compare the result before extending the change.

---

## Sector Notes: Logistics tech

- **A strong proof point here:** A before and after of on time delivery or cost per shipment on one lane, site or region, measured over a full cycle of busy and quiet weeks.
- **What readers in this sector measure:** on time delivery, cost per shipment or per order, order cycle time, exception rate, delay and damage claims, service level attainment, manual planning time.
- **Terms this sector's buyers use:** shipment, carrier, consignment, lead time, exception, service level, proof of delivery, third party logistics provider, transport management system, warehouse management system.
- **Your results:** they carry a figure.

## Check Before You Publish

- The customer has approved the story, every figure and the quote in writing.
- Every figure comes from the customer or a page you can cite; page claims stay labelled as the vendor's own claims.
- Nothing in the recognition or company-wide claims is shown as this customer's result.



## Reading the answer

This story supports a draft account of “Late deliveries down 60%, planning time cut from 4 hours to 30 minutes, 12% lower fuel cost”. Source verification and written permission for the exact wording remain separate checks. A single pilot is not proof of general or causal improvement. The conclusion needs review if the original records alter the baseline, measurement period or sample, or the customer declines the proposed wording or use.

## Decisions by role

Proposed owners. Confirm the named person before acting. Supplied statements below are inputs to check, not established findings.

Founder: ask the evidence owner to distinguish observation from attribution in “Late deliveries down 60%, planning time cut from 4 hours to 30 minutes, 12% lower fuel cost”; endorse only the supported scope.

CEO: ask the publication owner for written customer approval of “Late deliveries down 60%, planning time cut from 4 hours to 30 minutes, 12% lower fuel cost” and the intended channels; keep distribution on hold until it is recorded.

CMO: compare “Dispatchers spent four hours a day planning routes by hand and late deliveries hit 18 percent” and “Late deliveries down 60%, planning time cut from 4 hours to 30 minutes, 12% lower fuel cost” with the original records; retain sample and period in the final story before requesting approval.

CRO: ask the account owner whether “RouteIQ planned routes automatically and sent drivers live updates” explains the buyer's next decision; do not promise another account the same outcome.

Demand generation head: test a reader action to measure the starting point for “RouteIQ”; check the destination and permission before distributing the story.


Region context: Which region applies: India, Southeast Asia, Middle East, UK, Western Europe or North America? Add it to your description and rerun.
